newsitem.title: USA: Nine U.S. Southwest utilities consider forming ISO.
newsitem.headline: Nine U.S. Southwest utilities consider forming ISO.

text.p: A group of nine Southwestern electric utilities announced Friday they plan to study the feasibility of creating an Independent System Operator (ISO) for the region's power transmission lines.

The group, called Desert Southwest Transmission and Reliability Operator (Desert STAR), said in a statement it would focus on ensuring reliability, nondiscriminatory open-access and independent governance during the transmission to a more competitive wholesale and retail power market.

Initial members include: Tucson Electric Power Co, Arizona Electric Power Cooperative, Pinnacle West Capital Corp's Arizona Public Service Co, El Paso Electric Co, Nevada Power Co, Public Service Co of New Mexico, Salt River Project, Texas-New Mexico Power Co, and the Western Area Power Administration-Desert Southwest Region.
A series of regional public forums to discuss the idea will be held throughout the month of April and a feasibility study is expected to be completed in six months.
Two ISO's already are under construction in the West. California is designing its ISO, and in the Pacific Northwest, the Independent Grid Operator is in the pre-approval stage.
